name: Self-update from GitHub Releases
description: Sideloaded VSIX updater. Compares the installed extension version against the latest GitHub release tag, downloads the .vsix asset to a temp dir, installs it via workbench.extensions.installExtension, and offers a window reload. Exposed as the codeWorkbench.checkForUpdates command (Workbench brand view title-bar button + palette) plus a once-per-day silent check on activation. When an update exists, applyUpdateState() persists the tag, flips the codeWorkbench.updateAvailable context key (title-bar icon swaps cloud-download to arrow-circle-up) and sets a badge on the brand view. When the extension was installed from a gallery (Marketplace / Open VSX; isStoreInstall() reads the injected packageJSON.__metadata.source === 'gallery'), registerUpdateCommand() returns early: it sets the codeWorkbench.storeInstall context key (hides the title-bar update buttons), registers the two commands as an informational "VS Code updates it automatically" message, and never contacts GitHub. release.yml additionally publishes a store VSIX (enabledApiProposals stripped) to the Marketplace / Open VSX when the VSCE_PAT / OVSX_PAT secrets exist.
guidelines: Release tags are v<semver> and the asset is code-workbench-<semver>.vsix; release.yml bumps package.json on main so installed version == tag.
Keep the activation check throttled (globalState timestamp) - unauthenticated GitHub API allows 60 req/h per IP.
Silent mode must never surface errors or up-to-date toasts; only the manual command talks on failure.
Vitest imports src modules in a node env: 'vscode' is aliased to test/stubs/vscode.ts. Extend the stub rather than mocking per-test.
applyUpdateState() is the ONLY writer of the availableVersion key, the updateAvailable context key and the brand-view badge - keep them in lockstep by routing every set/clear through it.
The brand view is lazy: BrandViewProvider.setBadge() stores the badge and resolveWebviewView() re-applies it, so a badge set during activation survives first reveal.
Context keys and badges do not survive a window reload - registerUpdateCommand() replays the persisted tag on activation.
Store installs (gallery source) must never run the GitHub updater; sideloaded VSIX installs (source 'vsix') always do.
The store build must strip enabledApiProposals - the Marketplace and Open VSX reject proposed APIs; the GitHub VSIX keeps it.
anti_patterns: Do not check for updates on every activation - it burns the API rate limit and nags the user.
Do not derive the releases repo from packageJSON.repository - the updater hardcodes REPO (the manifest URL now matches, but the constant is the source of truth).
Do not set view.badge directly from outside BrandViewProvider - a badge assigned before the view resolves is silently dropped.
Do not treat the presence of __metadata.installedTimestamp as a store install - sideloaded VSIXes have it too.
decisions: Distribution: GitHub Releases + self-update for sideloaders, plus Marketplace / Open VSX publishing from release.yml when store secrets are configured; VS Code updates store installs natively.
'Skip This Version' is persisted in globalState and cleared whenever the user runs the manual check; skipping also clears the update-available icon and badge.
The title-bar icon swap is done with two when-gated menus.view/title entries on the same command rather than a second command, so the palette keeps one entry.
